subject: cold war control room
title: What If a Computer Said Five Nukes Were Coming? In 1983 One Did

scenes.text: What if a computer said five nuclear missiles were coming? On September 26th, 1983, one did.
scenes.keywords: cold war control room red alert screen

scenes.text: Just after midnight, a Soviet early-warning satellite flagged one American launch. Then four more. Five missiles.
Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov had about five minutes to report it. American missiles would land in roughly twenty.
Five missiles made no sense for a first strike, and ground radar saw nothing. He called it a malfunction.
The cause: sunlight glinting off high clouds, mistaken for rocket exhaust. Petrov was reprimanded over paperwork and quietly retired.
The world only learned in the 1990s. The man who may have prevented nuclear war died in May 2017, and nobody noticed for four months.

description:
What if a computer said five nuclear missiles were on their way? On 26 September 1983 the Soviet Oko satellite system reported five US launches, and duty officer Stanislav Petrov, with about five minutes to decide, judged it a false alarm.
The cause was sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds. The incident stayed secret until the 1990s; Petrov died in May 2017 and his death went unreported for months.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Petrov had no launch button; his job was only to report upward, and he reported a malfunction instead. Would you have trusted the screen? And what should we run through next?
